questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me I wanted to go the the US because of a personal connection to the country, but I mostly have been spending time in the north east so I wanted to try something now and Austin sounded very interesting

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: it was fairly easy by simply looking around on the websites they had introduced you to, plus talking with the other danes help alot

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: noting

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, for people who like big houses and a lot of parties I would go for college houses, if you like it a bit more quiet, small and homey then go with ACC

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: west campus is where most things happen so for a good student experiance i would live there if you just want a quiet place to live then north campus might be better

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: after being accepted you just had to accept and then the international office had a bunch of forms that you needed to fill out but is was pretty easy but time cunsuming

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: a phone number and an email adress but pretty long responds times

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: of the classes they offered that semester I got what I wanted but some of the classes I wanted they didn't even offer when I was there

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: as soon as possible find the course catalog for the specific semester you will be there

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the physics courses were below standard academically compared to denmark, and I had a course that was not at all what it was advertised to be

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: very different, very little class time compared to physics at UCPH and also a lot of remerization as all classes were closed book

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
partical physics
Discrete mathematics
american military history
Data analysis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
particle physics was a very good astro physics course

american military history, is very interesting if you are interested in military and history in general

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: all kinds, the international office did a lot of events, in sports they are one of the best in the US overall and you can play any sport you want

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: join a club or a sports team, you don't need to be hevely invested but it is a great why to make friends because it is hard to do that in the classroom

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: weekend trips to some of the other Texas cites were a fun experiance, and if you like hiking then big bend is the place to go

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I had no problems but have been in the US before

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: find friends at your house and in clubs or teams

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the food, you need to be careful as everything is just more unhealthy

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the hospitality

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
it is very hot, so from the beginning get used to carrying a water bottle
take some time to explore campus, it is very big and very place has its own vibe find one you like
east 6th street and rainy street are to great places to get a drink and experiance some live music

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: get your student ID as fast as possible, it gets you into must buildings and free public transport, butyou have to go online and order one yourself

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the friends i made along the way

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: trying to joggle everything, going out on the weekends, going to practise during school and friends it can become a lot

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
